questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most crucial aspect to me choosing Istanbul as a destination was that Turkish culture is very different from Danish culture, and that I wanted to learn more about the Turkish way of life. Istanbul has a rich history, which is apparent in historical landmarks, cultural institutions and religious buildings.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to personal issues I did not have the best study abroad experience, but the destination itself was very interesting and I learned many new things I would not have, if I had not chosen to go on exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Istanbul Bilgi University sent out an information package before my arrival. This was very informative with recommendations for housing, student clubs, cultural customs and so on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The International Student Office and the Erasmus Office at the main campus was able to assist with any questions I had about registering for courses and etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Due to covid restrictions, the university did not have any intro days or gathering with information upon arrival. This would have been useful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find housing on Air bnb, but the rent was very high compared to general prices. However, there are many Facebook pages such as 'Erasmus Istanbul' or 'Foreigners in Istanbul' where you can search for housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus can be a little pricy, however you gain more of an insight into Turkish way of living though renting off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing available through the university were small rooms and not very cosy.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process for courses at the university was a bit confusing and many had trouble getting into the courses that they wanted. Therefore I think that introductory days on campus upon arrival would have been useful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university sent out a guide for registering for courses. You had to have a student ID first however, and if you did not receive this in your mail, you had to go to the Erasmus Office, where the employees were helpful. Thereafter you registre through Bilgis system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help was available at the Erasmus Office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful in registreting for my classes, but you have to contact the professors prior to choosing the class, because not all classes were suitable for Erasmus students or taught in English even though it said so on their website with course descriptions.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact professors prior to choosing the course to make sure that it is suitable for you as an exchange student.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was lower than in Denmark in my experience.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was lower than expected. There were more weekly assignment and less bigger projects.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was more classroom oriented with smaller classes and more engagement between professors and students compared to UCPH. This was definitely positive and I was very satisfied with this part.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 'Issues in Cyberculture', 'Introduction to Post-Colonialism', 'History of Nationalism, Memory and Commemoration', and 'Femininity, Masculinity and Modernity'

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course 'Femininity, Masculinity and Modernity' as the professor was very engaged and the classes were interesting. I would also recommend 'History of Nationalism, Memory and Commemoration' as you learn a lot about Turkish history and their relationship with the rest of Europe.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Clothing and groceries were slightly more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were student clubs available, but they did not create awareness of how to get into these clubs. Many tried to contact the clubs, but never got a reply.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yoga and Volleyball

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any non-academic activities on campus. I found a ceramics course off campus that I enjoyed.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to the Prince Islands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust to the local culture, as Turks are very open and keen to share their culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There was created a whats app group, where events were posted and you could arrange meet ups with other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You can smoke inside a lot of places in Istanbul, which can be a bit unpleasant.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Turks are very open and easy to talk to. There are lots of cultural sights in Istanbul.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Find housing before you leave, even if it is just temporary. Once you are there it is easier to find a place through friends you meet and to figure out which areas you like the best. 2. You have to go to the Erasmus Office a lot to get set up with your courses in the beginning. 3. Engage and meet up with other students through the whats app groups.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't have to know everything before you leave.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding experience was meeting students from other countries, who were going through the same experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My greatest challenge was to make close friendships - but there are always other Erasmus students you can hang out with.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
